What the checks cover

Test coverage.

These are software regression checks of defined routes, events and state transitions.

AreaCheckExpected behaviour
Accessibility policiesStairs, escalators, slope and unknown attributesHard constraints exclude the affected graph edges.
Weather and objectivesDistance, shelter, indoor routing, effort and timeThe selected objective changes route cost and preference ordering.
Facility eventsClosure, restoration and alternate routesThe remaining route changes or returns a clear no-route state.
Photo workflowsObservation, map IDs and candidate confirmationOnly valid candidates from the current map can be applied.
Journey sessionsCommand versions, reconnection, reset and persistenceThe phone and console retain a consistent state.
Scene contractsManifest, graph, floor and facility referencesEach scene loads through the same validated schema.

Route recovery

Route recovery
examples.

Lift A closes

A confirmed closure targets Lift A. The event policy removes its affected edges, and the planner selects a remaining path through Lift B when that path is available.

A landmark resets the origin

Confirming the A-1 Bakery candidate moves the start anchor to the nearby LG1 public passage. The route is recalculated from that node.

Next measurements

Field evaluation.

A field evaluation can record journey completion, time to recover after a simulated closure, labelled-photo match accuracy and task-level model latency and cost.

The Kowloon Tong route provides a concrete setting for comparing these measures across mobility profiles.
